description:
Re-review finding (2026-07-03, joinorder Track-2 review triage). The canonical
JoinOrder data archive is not downloadable: the manifest URL
(benchbox/core/joinorder/data_manifest.toml:6,
`https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/releases/download/data%2Fjoinorder-imdb-2013-v1/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1.tar.zst`)
returns HTTP 404. The git tag `data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1` exists (at
0182c955, the v0.2.1 commit), but the GitHub API lists NO release object for
it -- the repo is public and an authenticated releases list shows only the
v0.x.x package releases. Every `JoinOrderBenchmark.generate_data()` call on a
cold cache therefore fails with `DownloadError ... returned status 404`
(verified 2026-07-03 in a clean environment), so canonical joinorder is
unusable for any user who has not previously cached the archive.

This contradicts the completed cutover item
(_project/DONE/main/planning/joinorder-canonical-cutover.yaml), whose
work/verification recorded "Promote DRAFT GitHub Release to published" and
"asset is publicly downloadable without auth" as done. Either the release was
never actually promoted, or it was deleted afterwards. The licensing decision
(_project/decisions/joinorder-canonical-data-licensing-2026-05-12.md:5,24)
explicitly accepted keeping the BenchBox-hosted archive as the default data
path, so absence is a regression, not a deliberate takedown -- if a takedown
WAS intended, that decision must be recorded and the manifest/fetch path
changed instead.

The same 404 was independently observed during ClickHouse server UAT and
deferred there (_project/TODO/main/planning/
uat-clickhouse-server-data-and-timeout-tail.yaml:18-19); this item is the
dedicated owner of the fix.

Only the project owner can restore the asset: the published archive
(`joinorder-imdb-2013-v1.tar.zst`, ~1.2 GB, sha256
`669c97ce7e9e7498c7ce0cad018153aa93a9b8eefff0f77e436d690f64ebc5fd` per the
manifest and _project/joinorder/release-notes.md:8) exists only in local
build/UAT caches, not in the repo.

RESOLVED 2026-07-09. The byte-identical archive was unrecoverable (no local
copy, no backup, non-deterministic rebuild), so the original "re-upload the
exact asset" plan (w1-w3) was superseded by
_project/decisions/joinorder-logical-verification-2026-07-08.md: adopt
logical row-content verification as the dataset identity, keep dataset_version
joinorder-imdb-2013-v1 (a transport-wrapper rebuild, logical content
unchanged), rebuild the archive via the foundation pipeline, and re-publish.
Outcome: manifest is logical-mode (per-table logical_sha256; logical
manifest_hash/data_archive_hash stable across future rebuilds); new archive
106ae78c published at tag data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1 (asset URL now 200, not
404); cold-cache generate_data() returns 21 tables and verify_logical_content
reports ALL_MATCH on the full 74M-row dataset.

anti_patterns.dont: change the manifest URL to a different host as a quick fix
anti_patterns.why: the licensing ADR evaluated the GitHub Release path specifically; a host change is a new decision.

anti_patterns.dont: regenerate manifest hashes to match a rebuilt archive without also regenerating reference_cardinalities.json and release-notes.md

preserves.behavior: The licensing posture: DATA-LICENSE.md ships in the archive and the redistribution disclaimer stays in _project/joinorder/release-notes.md.

data_manifest.toml hashes (archive_sha256, per-table sha256, manifest_hash) stay unchanged unless the uploaded archive genuinely differs -- in which case ALL dependent reference artifacts (reference_cardinalities.json, release-notes.md) must be regenerated together.

prior_art.concept: _project/DONE/main/planning/joinorder-canonical-cutover.yaml -- the original publish + UAT checklist; reuse its promote/verify commands.
_project/decisions/joinorder-canonical-data-licensing-2026-05-12.md -- the accepted-risk decision that authorizes hosting the archive.
benchbox/core/data_fetch/manager.py:fetch_data -- the download path that currently fails; no code change expected here.

verifications.description: Release asset URL resolves (302 to CDN or 200), not 404

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import tempfile; from benchbox.core.joinorder.benchmark import JoinOrderBenchmark; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); print(len(JoinOrderBenchmark(output_dir=d).generate_data()))"
verifications.description: Cold-cache canonical joinorder datagen succeeds end-to-end

work_units.notes:
Check the GitHub audit log / release history for tag
data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1. One line in this TODO's notes or the
release-notes doc is enough; the point is to know whether cutover w-item
verification was recorded without actually passing, since that affects
how much to trust the remaining cutover verifications.
work_units.summary: Determine why the release object is missing (never promoted vs deleted) and record it

work_units.notes:
From a machine that has the built archive (owner's build cache or a
rebuild via _project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py):
  1. Verify the local archive sha256 matches the manifest's
     archive_sha256 669c97ce7e9e7498c7ce0cad018153aa93a9b8eefff0f77e436d690f64ebc5fd
     BEFORE uploading; if it differs, the manifest/reference artifacts
     must be regenerated instead (they are hash-locked).
  2. gh release create data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1 <archive> (published,
     not draft) or gh release upload if the release object reappears.
work_units.summary: Re-publish the release at tag data/joinorder-imdb-2013-v1 with the archive asset

work_units.notes:
curl -sSI on the manifest URL must return 302/200 (not 404), and a
cold-cache `JoinOrderBenchmark.generate_data()` (or
`benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark joinorder --data-only`)
must download, extract, and sha256-verify all 21 tables. Update the
deferred note in uat-clickhouse-server-data-and-timeout-tail.yaml to
point at this completed item.
work_units.summary: Verify cold-cache fetch end-to-end and close the loop on the UAT deferral
